{
  "role": "code-review",
  "head": "60df907d432078e0edbda71568becdb5af6cd193",
  "base": "ad92a0864ac56987a4896fd5770abab0c0c9b271",
  "verdict": "request_changes",
  "signal": "fail",
  "summary": "The committed port has unresolved lifecycle and control defects: delayed finish commands can operate on a different group, profile responses can affect a later selection, and polling can indefinitely cancel slow requests.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/test-session-manager/test-session-manager.service.ts",
      "line": 360,
      "title": "Bind the delayed finish command to the original group and session",
      "evidence": "After locking the current group, the finish operation waits 1.5 seconds and then derives termination targets from the manager's current sessions. The subscription is not tied to the component lifecycle. If the operator changes groups during the delay, connect() replaces those sessions, so the pending operation can terminate participants in the newly selected group. A logout or other auth transition can also leave the delayed operation using the then-current credentials.",
      "recommendation": "Capture the intended group, access identity, and eligible target IDs when the operation starts; cancel or reject the continuation on group change, logout, or destruction, and ensure both requests use the same authorized context."
    },
    {
      "severity": "high",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/group-monitor.component.ts",
      "line": 131,
      "title": "Cancel stale profile requests and reset profile settings on selection",
      "evidence": "Each route change starts an independent profile subscription that is neither canceled nor associated with the selected route. A slower response for a previous profile can apply its filters and display settings after a later profile is selected. Existing profile filters and settings also remain when changing to a profile with fewer filters or to a route without a profile, potentially hiding participants or changing which sessions controls affect.",
      "recommendation": "Switch profile loading with the route, cancel stale work on route change and destruction, and reset profile-derived filters and display settings before applying the current profile. Add tests for out-of-order responses and profile-to-no-profile navigation."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/backend.service.ts",
      "line": 17,
      "title": "Do not abort every snapshot that takes more than five seconds",
      "evidence": "The five-second timer uses switchMap, whose next tick unsubscribes and aborts the preceding fetch. A server that consistently responds in six seconds never produces a snapshot, even though the HTTP deadline is 20 seconds; the cancellation is silent, leaving the monitor fetching indefinitely or displaying stale data.",
      "recommendation": "Allow an in-flight poll to finish within its configured deadline, for example by skipping timer ticks while a request is active or scheduling the next poll after completion. Test a response slower than the polling interval and verify cancellation still occurs on disconnect."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/booklet/booklet.service.ts",
      "line": 36,
      "title": "Do not permanently cache transient booklet failures",
      "evidence": "getBooklet converts fetch failures into BookletError values, and shareReplay(1) retains that value in the name cache. A temporary network failure or timeout on the first request therefore prevents subsequent successful polls from loading that booklet for the lifetime of the access identity, leaving its participant rows without the booklet data needed for rendering and controls.",
      "recommendation": "Evict failed booklet results or retry them with bounded backoff while retaining successful cache entries. Cover recovery after an initial failed request."
    },
    {
      "severity": "medium",
      "path": "rewrite-app/apps/web/src/app/native-monitor/group-monitor/group-monitor.component.ts",
      "line": 289,
      "title": "Return to an existing route after finishing the group",
      "evidence": "A successful finish navigates to /r/starter, but the rewrite router has no such route; its wildcard redirects to /home. The operator consequently leaves the native monitor for the rewrite home page instead of returning to monitor selection, while the native session remains stored.",
      "recommendation": "Navigate to the native monitor selection route, and cancel the delayed navigation if the component or session has changed in the meantime."
    }
  ],
  "verified": [
    "Confirmed the worktree HEAD is the requested commit and inspected the committed diff, native monitor source, routes, session handling, and relevant Original monitor code.",
    "Inspected the supplied validation evidence: it reports the configured-cache negative and positive proof, including 12 browser markers, and identifies the earlier 5d9 CI failure.",
    "Reviewed the literal signed-int64 parsing and command serialization tests, and the supplied session transition tests."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "This was a read-only source review; the supplied broad build and test results were not rerun.",
    "The supplied evidence does not establish CI qualification for this HEAD.",
    "The identified asynchronous and control scenarios were established from the code paths; they were not reproduced in a live browser during this review."
  ]
}
